subject: riotInterceptor
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: corporate riot-control interceptor with a water cannon and neon light bars.
Style: Cyberpunk 2077.

spec.name: Arasaka-Style Riot Interceptor RC-9 'Pacifier'
spec.description: A hulking cyberpunk corporate riot-control armored interceptor with a roof-mounted water cannon, neon light bars, riot shields and glowing corp emblems.
spec.layout: Low, wide, wedge-shaped armored 6-wheeled truck facing +Z. Front: sloped armored nose with a bull-bar/ram plate, a glowing cyan neon light bar across the grille and a red-amber LED strip bumper. Middle: a tall angular cab with a narrow slit visor windshield glowing magenta-tinted glass, side riot-shield panels, and roof light bars (cyan and magenta alternating). Rear: a raised tank deck carrying a rotating water cannon turret on a ring at the roof, plus a water tank with hazard stripes and hose reels, rear spoiler wing with neon edge. Six chunky wheels (three per side) with hubcaps glowing, wheel arches in dark steel. Style: Cyberpunk 2077 - dark gunmetal hull with panel seams and rivets, hazard yellow trim, hot magenta and cyan neon, corporate logo decals (SVG), grime paint near the wheels and underside, glowing parts via glow kit. Everything sits on wheels touching y=0.

parts.builds: Lower armored hull: lofted wedge body from y=0.45 to 1.55 with sloped nose, side skirts, wheel arches cut with dark arch rings, underbody plate, front bull-bar ram plate with hazard-stripe paint, red LED bumper strip and cyan grille light bar (glow), headlight clusters (white glow), tow hooks, side door seams, panelled() hull paint with rivets, grime paint gradient toward the wheels and underside, corporate emblem decals on the flanks and POLICE-style 'CORP SEC' lettering textures.
parts.attaches: Top face at chassisTop; wheel arches centred on the three axle mounts; cab sits on cabFloor; tank sits on tankDeck.

parts.builds: Angular armored cabin above chassis: faceted slab roof, slit visor windshield with magenta-tinted glass (glow), side riot-shield panels with hazard chevrons, small side slit windows, door handles, roof light bars alternating cyan and magenta (glow) with housings, antennas and a sensor dome, camera pods, mirror stalks with small neon edges, a dark roof armor plating with panelled paint, and a drawn SVG corp emblem on the roof hood.
parts.attaches: Floor at cabFloor/chassisTop; roof bars at roofBar; rear wall meets tank at z=-0.6.

parts.builds: Rear section: raised deck with water tank (horizontal lathe cylinder in blue steel with hazard stripe bands and gauge texture), hose reels with coiled hoses, pump housing with pipes, rear spoiler wing on struts with neon magenta edge strip (glow), tail lights as red neon bars, rear ramp/step, exhaust stacks, cargo racks with riot shields stored, the turret ring base plate at turretRing with rivets and warning lights.
parts.attaches: Sits on tankDeck mount at chassisTop; turret ring base at turretRing; front wall meets cab at z=-0.6.

parts.builds: Roof turret: rotating yaw base drum on turretYaw (steel, panelled), armored gunner shield half-dome with slit, pitching cannon on cannonPitch: thick barrel tube with tapering nozzle, brass fittings and bands, hazard-yellow ring bands, glowing cyan nozzle ring and water-pressure gauge (gaugeTexture), feed hose sweeping down to the tank, side mounted sensor and a small neon status LED strip, targeting camera. Barrel points forward (+Z) in rest pose.
parts.attaches: Base at turretRing on the tank deck; hose reaches the tank pump.

parts.builds: Six chunky armored wheels (radius 0.5, width 0.45) with lathe tires, faceted tread blocks via merged boxes, steel rims with bolts, glowing neon hubcap rings (cyan front, magenta rear), mud grime paint on tires, mud flaps, plus axles, suspension arms, shock absorbers with coil() springs and brake discs visible behind rims. Each wheel on its own wheel joint, axle along X.
parts.attaches: Axles at frontAxle, midAxle, rearAxle mounts, wheel centres at x=±1.15, y=0.5; tires touch y=0.

calls.reasoning:
I'll write buildWheels using the Ctx type provided by the module without a direct import, keeping the signature loose and following the existing template. I'm planning the wheel joint setup, like wheelFL positioned at x=1.15 with direction [1,0,0].

For each wheel, I'm designing a lathe-generated tire profile with radius 0.5 and width 0.45, using enough segments (16-24) so the circumference approximates a smooth circle closely enough to sit flush on the floor. Then I'm adding tread blocks as 16 merged boxes spaced radially around each wheel to simulate tire texture.

Working out the math for placing each tread block: computing its center position by rotating around the X axis so the block's radial direction aligns with the wheel's circumference, then adjusting the radius slightly (0.485 instead of 0.5) so the blocks don't clip through the floor by more than a negligible amount.

Now I'm designing the rim: a lathed steel disc with eight small bolt cylinders arranged in a ring, plus a glowing hubcap ring using neon cyan on the front and magenta on the rear, with a dark center cap.

Adding a thin cyan glow ring around the hub and a small center cap, then checking that the rim disc doesn't poke through the tire's flat face given their offsets — I need to adjust the tire profile width so the rim sits properly recessed.

I'm thinking the rim needs spoke windows to reveal a brake disc behind it, so I'll model the rim as a lathe ring with lip plus separate spoke boxes, then place a thin dark steel disc and caliper peeking through at the right offset and radius so it reads as visible without clipping through the tire.

Fitting the hub cap and glow ring so they sit on the spokes without clashing, then shifting the bolts out to the rim ring at a larger radius to avoid overlap. Now I'm planning mud flaps positioned behind each wheel.

Working out axle placement between the hull and wheel, checking whether the wheel inset into the arch leaves enough clearance for a visible rod section.

I'm now planning the suspension components: a stub axle, a triangular lower control arm connecting body to wheel joint, and a shock absorber positioned so it's partially visible through the wheel arch opening.

I'm thinking through the shock body coloring and joint setup for the wheel bones, then working out a mud paint function for the tires that blends rubber with brown mud based on height and noise, applying it consistently across the lathe and tread geometry.

For the rim I'll use the clockwork kit's steel metal and glow effects, considering whether to add sidewall decals or a hazard stripe trim ring near the rim lip for visual detail.

Instead of a complex sidewall label, I'll go simpler and add a textured mud flap with yellow chevrons and a neon logo, facing outward on the back/front of the flap using an appropriately oriented plane.

Mud flaps should mount to the body rather than the wheel, so I'll switch their joint reference accordingly. Now I'm setting up the wheel configuration table with per-axle names, offsets, and color assignments, picking cyan for the front axle and magenta for rear, with the middle axle also leaning magenta for contrast. I'm also pulling in geometry merge utilities to combine the flap meshes efficiently.

Writing tread block geometry...

Now I'm working out spoke geometry as thin radial boxes rotated around the wheel's axis and positioned at the correct radius, plus small bolt cylinders oriented along the X axis using rotations to align them properly.

For the brake disc, I'm sketching a lathed ring shape sitting just outside the tire's inner face, and placing a caliper box attached to the car body near the top of the disc rather than rotating with the wheel.

I'm reconsidering the caliper placement though, since at those dimensions it could visually collide with the spinning spokes; I'll shrink it and tuck it closer in so it peeks just slightly above the disc without clashing.

Now I'm working out the suspension geometry: placing lower and upper wishbone rods connecting the body to the wheel hub, then adding a steel stub axle that runs along the wheel's rotation axis, sized to stay hidden within the tire while still attaching to the wheel joint so it spins correctly.

I'm also adding a hub knuckle cylinder and building the shock absorber assembly, with a lower damper rod, a thin steel piston rod, and a brass coil wrapped around them using a sweep path for the spring geometry.

Checking my triangle budget for the coil: with too many turns and sides the mesh balloons past what's reasonable, so I'm trimming to fewer turns and fewer sides per ring to keep the total triangle count manageable across all six wheels.

Still adding up polygon counts, bolts and spokes push each wheel over budget, so I'm trimming lathe segments down to 16, cutting bolts to 6, and simplifying cylinder sides to keep the total near 8-9k before suspension and coils add their share.

Now I'm sketching mud flap geometry and placement, positioning each flap near the wheel base with a slight outward offset, grimy gradient paint, and a bracket rod connecting it back up to the hull since it floats outside the wheel radius otherwise. I'm also wiring up wheel hub joints and glow colors, keeping per-wheel part counts manageable alongside the suspension components.

I'm designing a small SVG texture for the flap with yellow chevrons and a magenta "CORP" label, mapping it onto a plane oriented to face outward with the correct up axis so the artwork reads correctly. Now I need to pull in mergeGeometries and start assembling all these pieces into the final build.
